tasks.short: Write, review and rewrite a program from a workflow chart

steps.what: File the workflow chart and the program ticket
Analyze symbolic logic on the workflow diagram
Draft a rewrite of programs from chart fields

loop.input: ticket fields and the workflow chart
loop.output: a rewrite that cites only those fields
loop.check: Every cited input or output is on the ticket
loop.stop: One pass, then stop; leave a blank where a field is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Symbolic logic on a diagram is not a fixed mail-merge

steps.what: Review and rewrite programs where logic fails
Run checks on the rewritten program version
Sign the rewrite and hand it to the developer

tasks.design: The software developer files a ticket on {PROJECT} with program id, inputs, outputs and a link to the workflow chart in {DOCS}. A bounded draft proposes a rewrite only from those fields. The computer programmer rewrites the logic, a {DATA_PLATFORM} check runs those cases, and the programmer signs one version after reading the report. A green check is not the signature, and a draft never merges or deploys.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts and program intent lived in separate documents and mail, so a draft could not show which field a line came from.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can carry program id, inputs, outputs and a chart link, so each drafted line can be tied to a field or left blank.
tasks.still_hard: Symbolic logic and subject-matter exceptions still need the programmer, and a green check does not prove the rewrite is right.
tasks.human_edge: The programmer decides whether the rewrite matches the chart and whether that version may leave the draft.

ambition.what: Rewrite the program when the workflow chart changes, instead of waiting for a release batch

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping a chart into code, more time on logic that the draft missed. The programmer can refuse a version whose numbers are not on the chart.

reach.task: Accept or return the signed program version
reach.learn: Which chart fields are covered and which the programmer left blank

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this work is mostly an editor, a chart and a review. The hard part is the logic, not the typing.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant needs a person to review, so a drafted rewrite stays a proposal until the programmer signs it.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe a small trial that was slower while people felt faster, so this task does not count a feeling of speed as time saved.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests, so a green check is not treated as proof the rewrite is correct.

assumptions: Focal role is the computer programmer. The task ends at a signed program version and its check report. Merging and deploying stay outside this task.

Input contract: program id, input names, output names, chart link, rule notes. Producer is the software developer. If the chart has no link, the programmer marks the ticket manual and does not run the draft.

Use the ticket and document templates already in place before custom code. The meeting share in the prior is high for this task. Time today sits on the chart, the editor and the review, not on a workshop.
A passing check is not acceptance. Acceptance is the programmer's signature on one version.
unknowns: Which chart store is the record.
Who may sign when the programmer is absent.
Which programs have no named inputs.
research_questions: What share of rewrites arrive with a current workflow chart?
How often is the first draft rewritten in full?

already_counted.description: Programmer rewrites weak logic in the draft
Programmer's rewrite of failed logic stays in this step

incremental.description: Keep chart field names aligned when a new program type appears
Developers correct tickets the draft rejects

approvals.approved_version: program version signed after this check report

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most charts are still free text, so the draft rarely fires and the programmer rewrites by hand. The high case assumes clean fields, but every rewrite still has a full review. A green check is not counted as saved judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Correct program errors and recheck the desired results

steps.what: Read the error and the desired program results
Draft a change that might correct the errors

loop.input: error id and the desired result
loop.output: one change that cites that error id
loop.check: The change cites the error id and does not add a second fix
loop.stop: If the desired result is empty, return nothing and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: The right edit for an odd failure is not a lookup on the error text

steps.what: Rechecking the program after the appropriate changes
Run the named recheck and store the results
Judge whether desired results are produced

tasks.design: A failing check lands on {PROJECT} with error id, program id and the desired results. A bounded draft proposes one change from that record. The computer programmer edits it and rechecks the program. A {DATA_PLATFORM} job reruns only the named cases. The programmer, not the job, decides that the desired results are produced. Nothing writes to a live system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Errors were free text in mail, so a later pass could not tell which result the change was meant to restore.
tasks.enabler_now: A check can store error id, program id and the expected result as fields a draft must cite.
tasks.still_hard: Odd failures and the judgement that the desired results really appeared stay with the programmer. A green rerun is not that judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The programmer chooses the change and decides the recheck shows the desired results.

ambition.what: Recheck a corrected error the same day, instead of parking it for a weekly pass

tasks.altitude: Known, coded errors take less hunting. The programmer still owns the change and can refuse a rerun that looks green but wrong.

reach.task: Retest the case the programmer marked fixed
reach.learn: Which error ids are signed off and which are still open

evidence.claim: Correcting errors in a mid-size firm is reading a failure, editing the program and rerunning it. Most of that editing does not follow a fixed script.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant needs a person to review, so a proposed fix is not applied by itself.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests, so a green recheck is not proof the program is correct.
Digest [S28] describes a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task has no unattended write to a live system.

assumptions: Focal role is the computer programmer. The task runs from a recorded error to a signed recheck or a stopped attempt. Deploying the change is a later act.

Input contract: error id, program id, failing case id, desired result text, last change id. Producer is the check run. If the desired result is missing, the draft does not run and the programmer works from the raw failure.
Configure the existing check job before custom code. The meeting prior overstates this task. Time today is on the failure screen, the editor and the rerun.
A green recheck does not replace the programmer's decision that the desired results were produced.
unknowns: Which failures already carry a desired result.
Who may sign a fix when the programmer is away.
Whether some programs cannot be rerun off the live system.
research_questions: What share of errors repeat a case id already on the ticket?
How often does a green rerun still get rejected?

already_counted.description: Programmer edits the proposed change before rechecking
Hands-on rechecking stays with the programmer

incremental.description: Add new case ids to the check list after repeated errors

approvals.approved_version: recheck decision for this error id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most errors have no desired result, so the draft does not run and rechecking stays manual. The high case assumes named cases rerun, but every change and every acceptance stays with the programmer. No live write is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Revise, repair or expand existing programs

steps.what: State requirements for revision of existing programs
Decide on repair or expansion of the programs
Draft the revision from the requirements fields

loop.output: a revision that quotes only those fields
loop.check: The draft names the program id and the change type
loop.stop: One pass; stop and leave the draft empty if change type is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: How far to expand a program is not a fixed template

steps.what: Repair existing programs where the draft fails
Check operating efficiency against the requirements
Sign the revision before any live apply

tasks.design: A requester submits program id, change type and the new requirements on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft prepares a revision only from those fields. The computer programmer repairs or expands the programs by hand, then signs one version. A sample check on {DATA_PLATFORM} runs only after that signature. The draft does not apply the change to a live system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived as mail prose, so a draft could not tell a repair from an expansion or see the efficiency target.
tasks.enabler_now: The form can force change type, program id and a requirement statement before any draft runs.
tasks.still_hard: Whether operating efficiency is actually better, and whether the expansion matches the new requirements, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The programmer decides repair versus expansion and signs the version that may be applied later.

ambition.what: Sign a small repair the day the requirement is clear, instead of holding it for a monthly release

tasks.altitude: The week moves from retyping requirements to judging them. The programmer can block a revision that has no signed version.

reach.task: Schedule the signed revision into a release
reach.learn: Which requirements are in the signed version and which were refused

evidence.claim: Revising an existing program in a mid-size firm is a short requirements note, an edit and a sample run. The edit is the bulk of the time.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant needs a person to review, so the revision draft is not the change that ships.
Digest [S11] reports a large field study with more completed tasks and a wide error margin, so that uplift is not used as this task's saving.
Digest [S28] describes a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unsigned revision is never applied to a live system.

assumptions: Focal role is the computer programmer. Directing someone else to type is in this task only as the programmer's decision. The other person's typing, if any, is not counted as the programmer's saving.

Input contract: program id, change type (revision, repair or expansion), requirement text, efficiency note, requester. Producer is the software developer. Empty change type or missing program id is returned, not drafted.
Test the workflow form before custom code. Meetings in the prior are mostly this decision, not a long workshop. Sample runs are not a production deploy.
unknowns: Who else may edit the program when the programmer directs the work.
Which programs have no sample inputs.
Whether efficiency is measured or only described.
research_questions: What share of revisions are small repairs versus expansions?
How often is the signed version different in kind from the request?

already_counted.description: Programmer edits a weak revision draft
Repair time stays with the programmer

incremental.description: Update the change-type list when a new kind of revision appears
Developers resubmit requirements the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: revision version signed before any apply

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requirements stay free text, so the programmer still reads mail and edits by hand. The high case assumes the form is used, but every repair and every signature stays manual. Applying the change on a live system is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write programs that track inventory or control equipment

steps.what: Describe the inventory job or the equipment job
Map tracking, storing and retrieving data fields
Draft software packages for the specific job

loop.input: job kind and the field map
loop.output: a package that cites only mapped fields
loop.check: Every field in the draft is on the field map
loop.stop: One pass; stop if the system id is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: Equipment rules in prose do not match a fixed field list

steps.what: Update and maintain programs controlling equipment
Run named sample checks against the field map
Sign the programs before a live job runs

tasks.design: The software developer files a job on {PROJECT}: job kind, system id, inputs and outputs, linked to the {ERP} or {OPS_SYSTEM} object it must read. A bounded draft proposes software packages from those fields only. The computer programmer updates and maintains the programs, signs one version, and a {DATA_PLATFORM} check runs named cases. The draft does not write inventory or move equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job requests named a screen, not the fields to track or the equipment commands, so a draft invented columns.
tasks.enabler_now: The operations record can supply system id and field names, and the ticket can require them before a draft starts.
tasks.still_hard: What the job should do when stock or equipment is in an odd state is still the programmer's call.
tasks.human_edge: The programmer decides the program matches the job and signs the only version that may later be applied.

ambition.what: Sign a small inventory or equipment change in the same week it is requested, not in the next project cycle

tasks.altitude: Less time rediscovering field names, more time on the job rules. The programmer can refuse a package that would write to a live system by itself.

reach.task: Place the signed version where the job can run
reach.learn: Which program version is signed and that it must not be applied unattended

evidence.claim: Programs that track inventory or drive equipment are written against a named system. The risky part is a write to that system, not the first draft.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant needs a person to review, so the package draft waits for the programmer.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests, so a passing job check is not proof the program is safe to run.
Digest [S11] reports a large field study with more completed tasks and a wide error margin, so this task does not book that uplift as hours saved.

assumptions: Focal role is the computer programmer. The task ends when a signed program version and its check exist. Starting the job on live equipment is out of this task.

Input contract: job kind (tracking inventory, storing, retrieving, or controlling equipment), system id, input fields, output fields, owner. Producer is the software developer, using names from the operations record. Missing system id stops the draft.
Read field names from the existing operations record before custom code. The meeting prior is high. For this task the time is on the job ticket, the editor and the check.
No step writes stock or sends an equipment command. A green check is not permission to run live.
unknowns: Which equipment has no safe sample mode.
Who owns the inventory fields the program reads.
Whether storing personal data needs a separate privacy check.
research_questions: What share of job tickets name a real system id?
How often does the signed program differ from the first draft?

already_counted.description: Programmer corrects the package draft before maintaining it
Maintaining the programs stays with the programmer

incremental.description: Add a job kind when a new inventory or equipment pattern repeats
Developers fix tickets that lack a system id

approvals.approved_version: program version signed for this job id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes job notes stay vague, so the programmer still discovers fields by hand. The high case assumes clean tickets, but writing, review and the signature all remain. Live inventory updates and equipment commands are not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The programmer spends less of the week retyping a routine change from a ticket, and more on logic, error causes, and whether a revision may be applied.
reach: Software developers receive a signed program version and the check report, instead of a chat fragment.
Systems administrators see which version is signed, and that a draft never writes to a live system.
skills_to_grow: Write ticket fields a draft can be checked against.
Read a check result without treating a green run as proof.
Keep a live system unchanged until this program version is signed.
role.ambitious_version: Every program change names its inputs, expected results and rollback, and none reaches a live system without the programmer's signature on that version.
